gaps.lead: As well as speaking fluent French, she also speaks Russian.
gaps.explanation: in addition to = as well as.

gaps.lead: Although she was exhausted, she carried on working.
gaps.explanation: despite/in spite of + -ing: despite being exhausted.

gaps.lead: I always hated pasta when I was a child, but now I cook it regularly.
gaps.sentence: I ___ pasta when I was a child but now I cook it regularly.
gaps.explanation: 'used to + infinitive' describes a past state or habit that is no longer true.

gaps.lead: The athlete insisted that she had never taken banned substances.
gaps.explanation: deny having + past participle denies an earlier action.

gaps.lead: People claim that this herbal tea cures colds.
gaps.explanation: X is claimed to + infinitive = people claim X does.

gaps.lead: He spoke slowly so that the interpreter could follow.
They have accused the mayor of corruption.
gaps.explanation: Active 'they have accused him of' becomes passive: has been accused of.

gaps.lead: Brian was really interested in North American history in his school days.
gaps.sentence: Brian ___ North American history in his school days.
gaps.hint: be interested in = have an ___ in
gaps.explanation: 'To be interested in' becomes the noun pattern: 'had an interest in'.
